html:
The Eritrean Railway is a narrow gauge line built by Italy from the port of Massawa up the escarpment to Asmara and on to the west, between 1887 and 1932.

It climbs about 2,300 metres in some 120 kilometres, through tunnels and over viaducts. It reached Asmara in 1911 and later Agordat and Biscia, and carried troops and goods for Italian Eritrea.

The line was torn up for its steel and its sleepers during the war of independence. After 1993, retired railway workers rebuilt the section from Massawa to Asmara by hand, using old steam engines, and it reopened in 2003 as a symbol of Eritrean self-reliance.
sum: The Eritrean Railway is a narrow gauge line built by Italy from the port of Massawa up the escarpment to Asmara and on to the west, between 1887 and 1932.
